questions.question: The demand for a normal good increases with ________ in the consumer's income.
questions.solution: In economics, normal goods are any goods for which demand increases when income increases, and falls when income decreases but price remains constant, i.e. with a positive income elasticity of demand.

questions.question: Short run marginal cost curve cuts the average variable cost curve from _______ at the minimum point of average variable cost.
questions.solution: The short-run marginal cost curve will at first decline and then will go up at some point, and will intersect the average total cost and average variable cost curves at their minimum points. The average variable cost curve will go down (but will not be as steep as the marginal cost), and then go up.

questions.question: "Forests" is listed in the _________ list given in the Seventh Schedule in the Constitution of India.
questions.solution:
Option **4** is correct, i.e. __**Concurrent**__.

 
• Through the **42nd Amendment Act of 1976** five subjects were transferred from State to Concurrent List.
 
• They were:
 
 
• Education
 
• Forests
 
• Weights & Measures
 
• Protection of Wild Animals and Birds
 
• Admin

questions.question: Which Fundamental Right in the Indian Constitution states that all persons shall be equally protected by the laws of the country?
questions.solution: Article 14 of the constitution states that, the State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.

questions.question: ________ was imprisoned for the rest of his life by Aurangzeb.
questions.solution:
• In 1657, Shah Jahan fell seriously ill, which set off a war of succession among his four sons.
 
• His third son Aurangzeb emerged victoriously.
 
• Shah Jahan recovered from his illness, but Aurangzeb put his father under house arrest in Agra Fort from July 1658 until his death on January 1666.

questions.question: Name the Commission that came to India in 1928 to reform India's constitutional system.
questions.solution:
Option **4** is correct, i.e. __**Simon Commission**__.

__
 
• The Simon Commission was formed in 1927 to fully assess India's political reforms.
 
• The **Simon Commission** arrived in India on **3 February 1928**__.
 
• There was no Indian leader in this commission, there was opposition to Simon Commission all over the country.
 
• The commission consisted of seven members under the joint chairmanship of **​Sir John Simon, and Clement Attlee**.

questions.question: _________ is an example of intrusive igneous rock.
questions.solution:
__
 
• Granite is an example of Intrusive Igneous Rocks.__
 
• Granite is a common type of felsic intrusive igneous rock that is granular and phaneritic in texture.
 
• Granites can be predominantly white, pink, or grey in colour, depending on their mineralogy.
 
• When molten magma cools it forms Igneous Rocks. 
 
• There are two types of Igneous Rocks. They are:
 
 
• Extrusive Igneous Rock.
 
• Intrusive Igneous Rock.
 
 
 
• Extrusive Igneous Rock: When Molten Lava reaches earth crust, it cools down rapidly and becomes solid and rocks formed in this process are called Extrusive Igneous Rock. Example: Basalt
 
• Intrusive Igneous Rock: When Molten Magam cools down deep in the earth without reaching the earth surface, these types of rocks are called Intrusive Igneous Rock. Example: Granite 
 
• Granite is an igneous rock that forms when magma cools relatively slowly underground. It is usually composed primarily of the minerals quartz, feldspar, and mica. When granite is subjected to intense heat and pressure, it changes into a metamorphic rock called **gneiss.**

questions.question: The longitudinal valley lying between lesser Himalaya and the __________ are known as Duns.
questions.solution: The longitudinal valleys between the lesser Himalayas and Shiwaliks are known as ‘Duns’ in the west and ‘Duars’ in the east. Dehra Dun, Kotli Dun, and Patli Dun are the important examples.

questions.question: The male sex organs in a flower is the ________.
questions.solution: The flower is the reproductive unit of some plants (angiosperms). Parts of the flower include petals, sepals, one or more carpels (the female reproductive organs), and stamens (the male reproductive organs).

questions.question: In animals like Annelids, Molluscs, organs have associated to form functional systems, each system concerned with a specific physiological function. This pattern is called ________ system level of organization.
questions.solution: In the organ system level of organisation, organs are associated to form functional systems, each system concerned with a specific physiological function. e.g., Annelids, Arthropods, Molluscs, Echinoderms and Chordates.

questions.question: Contact force is another name for _________.
questions.solution: A contact force is any force that requires contact to occur. Muscular force is force that results due to the action of muscles. It is a contact force, since there is a contact between the surfaces.

questions.question: The force of friction between two surfaces will increase if:

options.text: a layer of lubricant is kept between the two surfaces
the two surfaces are pressed harder
air gap is created between the two surfaces
irregularities on both the surfaces are removed

questions.solution: Since the force of friction is due to the interlocking of irregularities in the two surfaces which slide with respect to each other, it will increase if the two surfaces are pressed harder, because interlocking between the irregularities will increase.

questions.question: An absolute ________ contains the complete address of a file on the Internet.
questions.solution: A Uniform Resource Locator (URL), colloquially termed a web address, is a reference to a web resource that specifies its location on a computer network and a mechanism for retrieving it.

questions.question: A change in which **NO** new substances are formed is called __________.
questions.solution: Physical changes are changes affecting the form of a chemical substance, but not its chemical composition. A chemical change (chemical reaction) is a change of materials into other, new materials with different properties, and one or more new substances are formed.

questions.question: The property of metal by which it can be drawn into wires is called __________.
questions.solution:
• Ductility is when a solid material stretches under tensile stress. If ductile, a material may be stretched into a wire.
 
• Malleability, a similar property, is a material's ability to deform under pressure (compressive stress).
 
• If malleable, a material may be flattened by hammering or rolling.

questions.question: __________ is the number of deaths in the population during a given period.
questions.solution: Mortality rate, or death rate, is a measure of the number of deaths (in general, or due to a specific cause) in a particular population, scaled to the size of that population, per unit of time.

questions.question: ____________ scheme by the Central Government aims at setting up an organized rural Panchayat in order to make the villages more self-sustained.

options.text: Gram Uday Se Bharat Uday Abhiyan

questions.solution: 'Gram Uday Se Bharat Uday Abhiyan' (Village Self Governance Campaign) is a Central Government scheme to strengthen Panchayati Raj in villages and ensure social harmony in villages. It was launched on the occasion of 125th birth anniversary of Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar.

questions.question: Who discovered Circulatory System?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__William Harvey.__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• William Harvey (1 April 1578 – 3 June 1657) was an English physician. 
 
• He was the first known physician to describe the entire process of systemic circulation, including the property of blood being pumped to the body and brain by the heart and the rest of the body.
 
• William Harvey discovered the circulation of blood.
 
• William Harvey examines the arteries, demonstrating how their pulsation is controlled by the left ventricle's contraction, while the right ventricle's contraction propels blood into the pulmonary artery. 
 
• He calculates the heart's capacity, the amount of blood expelled by each pump, and the number of times the heart beats in a half-hour.

questions.question: Which country did India lose to in the semi-finals of the Men's Cricket World Cup 2015?
questions.solution: The 2015 Cricket World Cup was the 11th Cricket World Cup, jointly hosted by Australia and New Zealand from 14 February to 29 March 2015. Australia defeated India in the Semi-Finals. Australia defeated New Zealand by 7 wickets to win their fifth ICC Cricket World Cup.

questions.question: Buland Darwaza is located in?
questions.solution:
• **Buland Darwaza** or the "**Gate of Magnificence**", was built in **1601 A.D**. by Akbar to commemorate his **victory over Gujarat. **
 
• It is the main entrance to the palace at **Fatehpur Sikri,** a town which is **43 km from Agra.**

questions.question: Which of the following awards is given for distinguished service in any field including the service rendered by the Government servants?
questions.solution: Padma Shri (also Padma Shree) is the fourth highest civilian award in the Republic of India, after the Bharat Ratna, the Padma Vibhushan and the Padma Bhushan. Awarded by the Government of India, it is announced every year on Republic Day.

questions.question:
Which of the statements given below are correct?

1. The author of 'The Great Indian Novel' is A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.

2. The author of 'A Foreign Policy For India' is I.K Gujral.

3. 'Wings of Fire' is an Autobiography of A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.
questions.solution:
• **The Great Indian Novel** is a satirical novel by **Shashi Tharoor.**
 
• It is a** fictional work** that takes the story of the **Mahabharata**, **the epic of Hindu mythology**, and **recasts and resets it in the context of the Indian Independence Movement** and the** first three decades post-independence.**

questions.question: In April 2017, diplomatic ties were re-established after 37 years between Cuba and _________.
questions.solution: Cuba and Morocco in the third week of April 2017 signed an agreement to re-establish diplomatic ties after a gap of 37 years. The announcement was made by the Cuban Foreign Ministry.

questions.question: Nepal shares a border with which other country besides India?
questions.solution: Nepal is landlocked by India on three sides and China's Tibet Autonomous Region to the north.
